name: Debmalya Pal

headline: Trustworthy AI · Human-Centered AI · Language Models · Multi-Agent Systems
positioning: I study how language models and multi-agent systems reason, fail, and can be made more reliable — and I build the systems that put that understanding to work.
intro: M.S. Computer Science (Artificial Intelligence) student at UC San Diego, working on interpretability, LLM reasoning, and agentic decision-support — after more than three years as a production software engineer.
bio: I'm a Master of Science in Computer Science student at UC San Diego, working on trustworthy AI, AI safety, and interpretability — bridging that with over three years of production software engineering before graduate school.

My primary focus is on making AI systems transparent and reliable at the representational level: probing and steering internal model behavior, understanding failure modes, and building interpretability tools that hold up under real-world constraints.

Alongside, I work on AI agents and multi-agent systems, focusing on grounding them in trustworthy AI principles so that multi-agent behavior more closely resembles how humans actually deliberate and operate.

Before joining UCSD in Fall 2025, I spent over three years as a full-stack software engineer, working across backend systems, databases, automated data pipelines, and cloud-native development. I bring that same engineering discipline to research prototypes and production systems alike: grounded, scalable, and well-structured.
collaborationNote: I am open to collaborations that push trustworthy AI forward — making systems more accessible, inclusive, and genuinely helpful.
researchInterests: Language model behavior, reliability, and interpretability
